idea.title: Ahoy or hello
idea.summary: Alexander Graham Bell promoted 'ahoy' as the phone greeting while Edison pushed 'hello' in an 1877 letter, so the first word to an unseen stranger started as a fight.
hookOptions: People almost answered the phone by saying ahoy
Bell said ahoy. Edison said hello.
The first phone greeting was a ship word
sources: Wikipedia: Hello: Edison suggested 'hello' in an August 1877 letter to T.B.A. David of Pittsburgh, saying a shout of hello could be heard 10 to 20 feet away.
Wikipedia: Hello: Alexander Graham Bell, who patented the telephone, used and promoted 'ahoy' as the greeting.

scenes.say: People almost answered the phone by saying ahoy.
Alexander Graham Bell, who patented the telephone, pushed that greeting.
But in 1877, Thomas Edison wrote a letter suggesting hello instead.
He said a shout of hello carries ten to twenty feet.
Hello won, and became the first word you say to someone you can't see.

scenes.name: Lucky Spoon
scenes.say: Almost a hundred and fifty years later, strangers still open the same way.

post.caption:
Bell said ahoy. Edison said hello. Hello won, and it's still the first word you say to someone new. Which would you have picked?

Try your first word at randomtalker.com
